title: Negative actions: plural partitive object
summary: In a negative action sentence, a plural object takes plural partitive: En osta autoja. — I do not buy cars.
objectives: Choose plural partitive objects in supplied negative action statements.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose plural partitive objects in supplied negative action statements.
The negative frame is already provided. The object still keeps the intended plural meaning. A negative statement does not turn several things into one grammatical object form.
Use the complete plural alternatives shown. Focus on case and number rather than deriving an unfamiliar stem.
keyPoints: A plural object in this negative action statement uses plural partitive.

steps: A plural object in this negative action statement uses plural partitive.
En means “I do not” and works as the verb. en comes from ei: the first-person singular negative verb en.
osta means “buy” and works as the verb. osta comes from ostaa: the negative main-verb form osta-, without a person ending.
autoja means “cars” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep auto and add -ja: auto + ja = autoja.

näe means “see” and works as the verb. näe comes from nähdä: the negative main-verb form näe, without a person ending.
kirjoja means “books” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Replace final a with o, then add -ja: kirjo- + -ja = kirjoja.
